name: Slate Hill Cattle Company
old_description: At Slate Hill Cattle Company, we are committed to ethical cattle farming and sustainable ranching practices while raising premium Pinzgauer beef. Our Pinzgauer cattle are known for their resilience, adaptability, and superior beef quality, which is enhanced by our focus on humane treatment and environmentally responsible methods.
about:
Slate Hill Cattle Company operates from Portsmouth, Rhode Island, on Aquidneck Island. The ranch was founded by Dennis Welch, a U.S. Navy veteran who moved to the state in 2006 for engineering work at Naval Station Newport. After marrying Crystle, a native of the island, the couple built a family-run operation rooted in the cattle-raising traditions Welch learned on Oklahoma ranches in the Ozark foothills.

The company raises Pinzgauer cattle on a grass-fed, rotational-grazing system that emphasizes soil health and biodiversity. Beyond premium beef, the ranch practices zero-waste utilization: suet is rendered into tallow for cooking, skincare, and candle making, while organs are freeze-dried into custom dog treats. The herd is managed with a blend of traditional husbandry and modern technology to monitor herd health and resource efficiency.

Products are marketed directly to consumers seeking ethically raised beef and natural pet treats, with an emphasis on local and regional customers who value transparent, sustainable sourcing.

Welch frames the venture as a family affair dedicated to preserving the Pinzgauer breed and ranching heritage for future generations. The operation’s stated goals include reducing its carbon footprint, expanding educational outreach on sustainable farming, and advancing regenerative practices to serve as long-term stewards of the land.

name: Smack Apparel
old_description: Since 1998, we’ve been making bold, unlicensed, and unapologetic gear that turns heads, starts conversations, and pisses off rival fans—in the best way possible.
about:
Smack Apparel was founded in 1998 in Tampa, Florida, by sports enthusiasts who wanted to create bold, unlicensed fan gear that sparks conversation at tailgates. The company operates its own screen-printing facility in Tampa, where it designs and produces all of its apparel.

The product line spans adult t-shirts (short and long sleeve), baby onesies, and toddler gear covering college football, professional football, and professional baseball. A separate Bushwood Prints collection offers fine art prints and tumblers featuring artwork by David O'Keefe. All garments use 100% cotton, 6 oz preshrunk fabric and are printed in-house; sizes range from small to 5XL.

Smack Apparel sells directly to end consumers via its website, targeting fans of specific programs such as Notre Dame, Michigan, Florida State, and professional teams like Chicago football. The company also serves parents and gift buyers with its Rookie Wear infant and toddler line. Products are explicitly unlicensed, with the company stating they are "licensed only by the 1st Amendment."

The brand differentiates itself through domestic production, original designs that lean into rivalry humor, and a fan-first voice that avoids corporate licensing restrictions.

name: Smart Cabling Solutions
old_description: Singlemode, Multimode, Armored, Outside Plant, Fusion splicing
about:
Smart Cabling Solutions, Inc. is based in Olathe, Kansas, and was founded in 2001 by Ron Wagner. The company began with a focus on personalized, hands‑on service for commercial network infrastructure. In the same year, Brian Koester, an RCDD‑certified Vice President of Operations, and Jeff Cox, Vice President of Business Development, joined the leadership team, helping the firm build long‑term relationships with customers, vendors, and manufacturers.

The company provides a full range of low‑voltage installation services: structured copper cabling (Cat 5e, Cat 6, Cat 6A, coaxial), fiber‑optic cable installation (singlemode, multimode, armored, outside‑plant) with fusion splicing using factory‑polished pigtails, data‑center build‑outs (cabinets, racks, wire management, ladder and cable tray), wireless access‑point and network‑equipment deployment, and removal of abandoned cable. Technicians use Fluke Versiv DSX‑8000 and Link IQ testers, calibrated annually, and multiple Fujikura and Fitel fusion splicers. Projects span facilities from 50,000 sq ft to over 1 million sq ft.

Smart Cabling serves warehousing and distribution, manufacturing and industrial, healthcare, corporate offices, education, and data‑center clients. Its customers include business owners, general contractors, IT professionals, and facility managers who need standards‑compliant infrastructure that supports current technology and future growth.

The firm differentiates itself through its Cat 6A expertise (thousands of Cat 6A cables and jacks installed), a fusion‑splicing process standardized since 2007, manufacturer‑backed warranties as a Commscope (Systimax/Uniprise 20‑year) and Leviton (lifetime) business partner, and a quality‑assurance program that includes documented testing, clean installations, and adherence to ANSI/TIA/EIA standards.

name: Smart Food NY Inc.
old_description: We specialize in seamless foodservice supply, connecting quality products with businesses efficiently. And we’ve been doing it since 1982.
about:
Smart Food NY Inc. operates from Manhattan, New York, serving the New York metropolitan area. The business traces its roots to 1981 when it was founded as Smart Distributor, and it has been operating under the Smart Food NY name since 1982. Ownership details and founder names are not publicly disclosed.

The company functions as a wholesale food distributor and cash-and-carry supplier, offering same-day and next-day delivery across the metro region. It sources products both globally and locally, with perishable items procured from the tri-state area. Its catalog spans coffee and tea, eggs and dairy, drink supplies, food supplies, plastic and paper supplies, baking supplies, and aluminum supplies. A notable product is a custom Martinson coffee blend that has been served since 1951.

Customers include cafes, bakeries, grocery stores, supermarkets, offices, restaurants, and other distributors throughout the New York Metro Area. The company emphasizes consistent taste and service for both long-standing and new accounts.

Smart Food NY highlights competitive pricing without sacrificing quality, fast local delivery, and products as its key differentiators. It began as a Chinatown wholesale food distributor and has maintained a focus on reliable supply for metro New York businesses.

old_description: Smart Sky Solar, the best solar installation company in Illinois, offers both grounded and rooftop
about:
Smart Sky Solar is a solar installation company based in Schaumburg, Illinois. Founded in 2006, the firm has served Northern Illinois for nearly two decades. Ownership details are not publicly disclosed, and the founders are not named in available sources.

The company designs and installs custom solar energy systems for residential and commercial properties, including ground-mounted and rooftop arrays. It also integrates solar-powered EV charging stations and battery backup systems for outage protection. Smart Sky Solar handles system design, permitting, and assists customers with federal tax credits and local incentives. The company reports completing over 1,000 projects and serving more than 1,000 clients since inception.

Its customer base spans homeowners seeking to reduce electricity bills and businesses aiming to cut operational energy costs by 50–75 percent. The firm also serves property owners adding EV charging infrastructure. All work is focused within the Northern Illinois region.

Smart Sky Solar emphasizes a customer-centric approach, transparent pricing, and the use of environment-friendly equipment that avoids roof damage. The company cites its team of veteran installers and a mission to accelerate clean energy adoption as key differentiators. about:
Smith Farms Custom Furniture operates from Murrieta, California, serving clients across Southern California including Temecula, Orange County, and San Diego County. The company was founded by Matt Smith, continuing a family tradition of woodworking craftsmanship. While the exact founding year is not publicly stated, the business emphasizes its heritage through the tagline "Continuing the Tradition."

The shop designs and builds custom furniture pieces such as dining tables, desks, chairs, beds, and occasional tables. Working primarily with premium hardwoods — including walnut, cherry, white oak, elm, ebo, and wenge — the team produces small-batch and one-off items. Recent projects highlighted on their site include the Willow Loft Bed, the Summer Olive Occasional Table, and the Wright Dining Table, each crafted from selected slabs and lumber.

Smith Farms serves residential clients directly, often collaborating with homeowners to tailor pieces to specific spaces and styles. A testimonial from a client in Fallbrook describes a collaborative design process where ideas are exchanged until the final solution matches the client's vision. The company's service area spans cities from Aliso Viejo to Valley Center, indicating a regional focus in Southern California.

The company differentiates itself through design recognition: its projects have earned awards from the New York Product Design Awards and the European Product Design Awards, including gold and silver honors for specific pieces. Features in Mountain Living Magazine, Western Design Conference, and other design publications underscore its reputation for award-winning custom furniture that blends functionality with aesthetics.

Smith Food Machinery was founded in 1996 in Stockton, California, by Ed Smith. The company remains family-owned and operated, focusing on brokering and selling quality used food processing equipment.

The firm acts as a broker and dealer for used machinery across more than 15 equipment categories — including conveyors, kettles, fillers, roasters, and packaging lines. Its inventory has included items such as Rietz disintegrators, Vanmark wash lines, FMC pulper-finishers, and Fuji robotic baggers. The company reports over 500 machines sold since inception.

Smith Food Machinery serves six core food sectors: nut processing, fruit and vegetable, bottling and beverage, filling/canning/labeling, confectionery, and packaging. Its customers range from dealers, brokers, and consulting engineers to end-user production plants seeking specific machines or surplus liquidation services.

The company emphasizes a no-pressure, personal-service model: every machine is vetted before listing, and buyers are invited to inspect equipment in person. Long-term relationships with a network of dealers and brokers are prioritized over one-off transactions.

old_description: Smith has been helping companies with tailored sourcing solutions since 1984
about:
Smith operates as an independent electronic-component distributor headquartered in Houston, Texas, with additional global hubs in Amsterdam and Hong Kong. The company was founded in 1984 and has accumulated more than four decades of experience navigating the semiconductor supply chain. No specific founder names or ownership designations such as family- or veteran-owned are disclosed in public materials.

The firm provides procurement, supply-chain management, and quality-testing services for electronic components and peripherals. Its service portfolio includes vendor-managed inventory, obsolescence management, excess-inventory recovery, custom supply-chain programs, and a proprietary trading platform called SmithTrade™. Smith reports shipping approximately 6.5 million parts daily, capturing 15 million high-resolution component images via its Argus™ visual-inspection AI since 2025, and operating five global operational facilities with in-house testing laboratories on three continents. Revenue for the first half of 2026 exceeded $6 billion.

Smith serves customers across aerospace and defense, automation, automotive, computing, consumer electronics, data center, e-commerce, education, gaming, IoT, medical, mobile, and oil and gas sectors. Its aerospace and defense work is supported by ISO/IEC 17025 AS6171 accreditation for authenticity testing.

The company differentiates itself through its 'Intelligent Distribution' model and a quality framework built on four pillars—Comprehensive, Consistent, Continuous, and Certified—supplemented by proprietary software, global logistics hubs, and a team of developers that customize IT integrations for each program.
